Going up leaves no safe move afterwards; going down, the next 3 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (2,4). So the line goes left.
The line must go up: down is number 8, which comes later.
Cell (2,5) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes right.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes up.
Going around the edge to (5,4), the next 3 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (4,1). So the line goes left.
The line must go left: around the edge to (5,3) is number 10, which comes later.
Going around the edge to (5,2) would strand number 7: it would be left with only one free neighbour. So the line goes left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes around the edge to (5,1).
Going right would leave number 8 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes up.
The line must go around the edge to (4,5): right is number 9, which comes later.
Going down would wall in number 11, the last number. So the line goes left.
Number 9 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!
